## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `74265b5f4ff6b3b6304d82f7dd15753fa3660258`
Local-runs: none
Scope: AGENTS.md, .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/queue-duration-budget.yml + scripts/ci/queue-duration.mjs, scripts/ci/queue-budget.json, docs/agents/build-and-test.md

Read: card #35322 body and its three comments (claim 6999763710, release 7005096299, claim 7014193859; no earlier record, no ruling comment beyond the card's own Source line), PR #35582 body and 6-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `b65488a8`), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff read to judge it: `scripts/ci/nightly-tiers-card.mjs`, `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`, the ten workflow files naming `merge_group`, the header of `docs/agents/build-and-test.md`.

### ① Derived judgments

- No package, schema or spec accept-set changes; nothing in any `files[]`. Right.
- One new workflow, `Queue Duration Budget`: schedule, `workflow_dispatch`, and `pull_request` paths-filtered to its own three files; no `merge_group:` and no `pull_request_target:`; top-level `permissions: {}`; not a required context. Right, and it agrees with the card's item 3 and with the AGENTS.md sentence that a gate grading a duration reports and never reds a required job.
- One new write identity: an issue with the fixed title `merge queue over its speed budget` and the body marker `os-queue-duration-budget`, labels `tooling`, `area:fleet`, `domain:devx`, `priority:p2`, `pm:queue` and type Task on create only. Matches the card's item 3 label for label. Right.
- The only write path is the `file` job, gated on verdict `over`, event not `pull_request`, ref `refs/heads/main`. On this head's own run `File or refresh the speed-up card` concluded skipped while `Read the merge-queue duration` concluded success. Right.
- `queueWorkflows` lists CI, Governed Surface Guard, Lint & Type Check, PR-Body Guards, Spec Liveness Check. On the head exactly those five workflow files carry a `merge_group:` trigger (the other five files that mention it carry it in comments only), and the names match each file's `name:`. Right.
- `budgetMedianMinutes: 22`, `alarmP90Minutes: 32` and the baseline are the card's numbers. Right. `minSample: 20` is a number the ruling does not give: it only turns a thin week into NOT MEASURED, never into a verdict, and it sits in the maintainer-owned file. Accepted, named here so the maintainer sees it.
- The verdict is `over` only when a value is strictly above its number; exactly 22 and exactly 32 read `within`. Agrees with the card's "exceeds". Right.
- `lint.yml` gains one sub-second offline self-test in the moved-bodies collector, so it runs on every pull request and every queue entry. Right; the comment says honestly that it is not a moved body.
- hotcrm is read report-only: `judge` answers `report-only` before any threshold, and the step is `continue-on-error`. Right.
- AGENTS.md gains a pointer, not the card's sentence. Wrong against the card's item 4: see S1.

### ② Semver level

Nothing published: `scripts/ci/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, `docs/agents/**` and `AGENTS.md` ship in no package. `skip-changeset` is correct and `Check Changeset` is success on the head. `Clause-②: no` is correct: no consumer-facing capability is added, narrowed or removed. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (who retires #35343): answered by events. #35343 was closed at 2026-11-19T16:25:42Z; `PR-body guards` re-ran on this head and concluded success (check-run 135708632864). The earlier red run (135703819224) had ONE error, the Duplicate Fix Guard naming #35343; its other three steps (closing-target-claim, partof-closing-keyword, single-claim-paths) each printed their pass line. So the duplicate was the only cause.
- For the seat, outside the diff: both guard runs warn `UNDETERMINED` on `check:closing-target-claim` because the newest `Claim:` comment on the card (7014193859) has no parseable `Branch:` line; the parenthetical after the branch name is the likely cause. The seat corrects the claim comment; it is a warning, not a red.
- Deviation from the card's item 4 (AGENTS.md carries a pointer instead of the sentence): not accepted as recorded, graded S1 below. If the fix needs the line ceiling raised, that is the maintainer's ruling, and the seat escalates it rather than choosing.
- `workflow_dispatch` NOT MEASURED: accepted as a limit of the platform, since a dispatch runs only a workflow on the default branch. The Done-when's two halves are covered as far as a pull request can: the head's own `pull_request` run took a live reading and skipped the write, and the de-dup is proven offline by the self-test inside `Lint & Repo Gates` (success). The seat owes one dispatch on `main` after merge and cites its run.
- For the maintainer: the PR's live reading has p90 32.1 against the 32-minute alarm, so the first run on `main` files the speed-up card. That is the design working, not a fault.
- Human Minimum box 3 (`pnpm lint` left to CI): answered by the head, every `Lint` and `Type Check` check-run is success. The CONTRIBUTING box is unticked and stays the dev's.
- `Rule-change: ruled` cites the maintainer's thread statements of 2026-11-19, the same Source line the card carries, not a ruling record id; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success on the head. Tier H approval is still owed by the maintainer, and the PR is a draft.
- Size: `size/xl` on an M card; `Check PR Size` is success. The bulk is the 270-line self-test and the card writer the Done-when asks for. Accepted.
- Card writer bounds, read against the live repo: 462 open issues plus 52 open PRs, so the 10-page scan completes with about half its bound to spare; no open issue carries the marker or the title today. The title-or-marker predicate and the bound are copied from `scripts/ci/nightly-tiers-card.mjs` unchanged.
- SQL push-down: not applicable, the diff touches no data path.
- Security-shaped findings: none.
- Check-runs on the head at record time: all completed ones are success or skipped except the superseded red run above. NOT FINISHED: `Test UI (1/16)`. This record does not cover its conclusion.

### ④ Design judgment

**AGENTS.md and docs/agents/build-and-test.md**

S1 (should-fix) — the card's item 4 puts one rule sentence in AGENTS.md: the queue has a budget, read weekly, over budget files a card, and a PR that changes CI or adds a gate reports the affected job's before/after median as advisory. The head puts `Queue speed budget: scripts/ci/queue-budget.json.` there, which names a file and states nothing to do or never do, and it puts the whole sentence in `docs/agents/build-and-test.md`. That page's own header, unchanged by this PR, says every paragraph below moved there verbatim out of AGENTS.md, that AGENTS.md carries every rule, and that where a paragraph reads as a rule the AGENTS.md sentence is the binding spelling. The new section was never in AGENTS.md, it reads as a rule ("A PR that changes CI or adds a gate reports its job's before/after median in its body"), and AGENTS.md has no sentence for it. So by the repo's own contract the reporting obligation the maintainer ruled binds nobody, and the companion's header is now false about its own content. The pointer also carries no link to the new section, unlike every other pointer in Build & Test. Fix, either way: the obligation gets its binding spelling in AGENTS.md (the free bytes on that line can carry the obligation plus a link instead of the bare path, or a ruled one-line ceiling raise lands the card's sentence), and the companion keeps only the explanation. The line itself is within the ratchet: 1050 lines, equal to `main`, and the edited line is under 120 bytes.

**.github/workflows/queue-duration-budget.yml**

Holds against the card and against the code it calls. Tried to break: a pull request cannot write (event guard, ref guard, and `issues: write` exists only on the `file` job); a step timeout leaves `exit_code` empty, which the last step treats as not `0` and reds; a NOT MEASURED reading leaves `verdict` other than `over`, so nothing is filed; `cancel-in-progress: false` keeps a filer from dying between its scan and its create; a `measure` that fails after the reading still lets `file` run, and `file` then reds at the download if the artifact is missing, never silently. Action versions match the ones the rest of the tree pins. The reason given for a separate file (the frozen `pull_request` paths list in `scripts/check-platform-checklist-watchdog.mjs`) is true of that script. The cron comment is true: no other workflow is scheduled at hour 07 exactly, though two run every four hours and one every six, none at 07.

N1 (nit) — the two read steps are bounded at 12 and 8 minutes and the job at 20, so two slow reads leave no time for the summary and artifact steps. On this head the objectstack read took 6 min 54 s of its 12. It fails loudly either way.

**.github/workflows/lint.yml**

Holds. The new line sits in a collector whose step ran inside `Lint & Repo Gates` (success), the closing echo's count was raised with it, and the comment states the one way this entry differs from its siblings.

**scripts/ci/queue-duration.mjs**

Agrees with its header and the card on: grouping by head SHA; green, red, cancelled, running and other; first `created_at` to last `updated_at`; nearest-rank percentiles; the failure rate over completed SHAs; the critical run and its five slowest jobs over 40 evenly spaced green SHAs; exit 2 for NOT MEASURED and exit 0 for an OVER week; the token read and never printed; `fileQueueCard` refusing any reading that is not `over`, refusing an unfinished scan, refreshing the oldest match in place, and never touching labels on a refresh. The self-test has a declared roster, a floor of 8, per-battery floors and the reached-verdict handshake that AGENTS.md "Writing a --self-test" asks for.

S2 (should-fix) — `listQueueRuns` does not keep its own sentence, "listed whole or refused". After the paging loop nothing compares `got.length` with `total`: a first page shorter than 100 rows under a larger `total_count`, or a later page that comes back short before the total is reached, ends the slice and the short list is accepted as the reading. The function's comment says why that matters: a truncated list reads as a faster, smaller queue. The self-test proves only that a page that throws fails the listing. Fix: refuse a slice whose rows fall short of its `total_count`, with one self-test case for the short page.

N2 (nit) — each SHA's duration is rounded to a tenth of a minute before the percentile is taken, so the budget is judged at that resolution: 22.04 reads as 22 and `within`.

N3 (nit) — a SHA is green on the queue-workflow runs the window holds for it; nothing requires all five to be present, so a SHA cut by the window's start edge is measured short. Negligible at 1837 green SHAs.

**scripts/ci/queue-budget.json**

Holds: the ruled numbers, the baseline with its window, the five workflows, and a `note` that the validator requires to name the maintainer.

Two open findings, S1 and S2, each owed a delta review of its fix. No must-fix.
